title: reduce GPU memory and workspace: activation checkpointing, arena tuning, scratch buffer reductions
author: Ethan Ramirez
release_notes: Reduced peak GPU memory and workspace allocations by tuning activation checkpointing, scratch buffer lifetimes, and arena allocation heuristics. No API changes.
description: Context: Production workloads showed increased OOMs and higher p95 GPU memory usage for certain long-context chat models under continuous batching. Motivation: Reduce peak GPU memory footprint and transient workspace allocations without regressing latency or throughput. This PR implements a set of coordinated runtime changes: 1) make activation checkpointing adaptive per-layer (only enable for layers where recompute cost < workspace savings), 2) move ephemeral scratch buffers to a per-stream scratch arena with LRU reuse and delayed free, 3) refine the GPU memory arena tuning heuristics to prefer compacting small lifetimes into shared slabs, 4) schedule KV-cache allocation to prefetch into sub-allocations to avoid large contiguous workspace spikes during multi-request merging. Results: end-to-end benchmarks (see bench summary below) show 18-32% peak GPU memory reduction across tested LLMs (small -> medium variants) and 10-12% reduction in average workspace allocations under continuous batching while maintaining p99 latency within SLOs. Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked (ENG-9012) - [x] Benchmarks run (local perf-canary + nightly) - [x] Unit + integration tests added - [x] Reviewed by runtime and infra - [x] Release notes drafted Changes in this PR are implementation-level and do not require customer changes.
commit_summary: Initial heuristic for adaptive activation checkpointing; baseline-on and threshold parameters (commit)
Introduce per-stream scratch arena with LRU reuse and delayed free path
Refine arena allocator: slab sizing and compaction heuristics to reduce fragmentation
KV-cache sub-allocation scheduling to reduce contiguous allocation spikes during batching merge
Add unit tests for arena reuse and checkpointing decision logic
Benchmark harness updates and perf results summary file
benchmarks_summary: Model: redwood-small (seq_len 4096, batch 8) -> peak GPU mem down 18%
Model: redwood-medium (seq_len 8192, batch 4) -> peak GPU mem down 27%
Continuous batching mixed load -> avg workspace allocations down 10-12%
End-to-end throughput change: +0-3% (within noise) depending on packing), p99 latency within 5% of baseline
